First, calculate the moles of each species.

\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}:&\;0.5\ \text{L}\times0.1\ \text{M}=0.05\ \text{mol}\\
\text{HCl (strong acid)}:&\;0.4\ \text{L}\times0.2\ \text{M}=0.08\ \text{mol}\\
\text{Ba(OH)}_2\ (\text{strong base}):&\;0.3\ \text{L}\times0.3\ \text{M}=0.09\ \text{mol}\\
&\text{gives }2\times0.09=0.18\ \text{mol OH}^-
\end{aligned}
\]

**Neutralize the strong acid with the strong base**

\[
\text{OH}^-_{\text{excess}} = 0.18 - 0.08 = 0.10\ \text{mol}
\]

**Neutralize the weak acid with the remaining OH⁻**

\[
\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O}
\]

All 0.05 mol of acetic acid are consumed, leaving

\[
\text{OH}^-_{\text{final}} = 0.10 - 0.05 = 0.05\ \text{mol}
\]

The total volume after mixing is  

\[
V_{\text{total}} = 0.5 + 0.4 + 0.3 = 1.2\ \text{L}
\]

\[
[\text{OH}^-] = \frac{0.05\ \text{mol}}{1.2\ \text{L}} = 0.0417\ \text{M}
\]

\[
\text{pOH} = -\log_{10}(0.0417) \approx 1.38
\]

\[
\text{pH} = 14 - \text{pOH} \approx 14 - 1.38 = 12.62
\]

The acetate formed is a weak base, but its contribution is negligible compared with the excess OH⁻.

**Correct choice:** (C) 12.62  

Answer: C
